questions.q: How are quick-service restaurants using AI?
questions.a: QSRs use AI in voice ordering at the drive-thru, in hiring and scheduling, and in managing guest feedback. Brands like McDonald's, White Castle and Lee's Famous Recipe Chicken run these tools across many locations in workflows that used to rely on people. The common goal is saving money, driving sales or making operations simpler.

questions.q: What does voice AI do in a drive-thru?
questions.a: Voice AI takes drive-thru orders so your team can focus on preparing food and serving guests. These systems are designed to reduce order errors, handle peak-time volume and speed up each transaction. Paired with AI-powered upsells, they can help grow sales as well as cut costs.

questions.q: How can AI help QSRs with hiring?
questions.a: Hiring automation screens resumes, schedules interviews and adapts to your staffing needs as they change. That shortens the time from an open position to a new hire's first shift. Your managers spend less time on paperwork and the rest of the team avoids the burnout that comes with running short-staffed.

questions.q: How does AI help restaurants manage customer feedback?
questions.a: AI pulls reviews and feedback from every location into one system, spots patterns, helps you respond within minutes and flags unhappy guests so you can recover them before they leave. Momos brings review management, insights, recovery and loyalty workflows together on one platform for multi-location brands. Turning feedback into retention protects your reputation and extends each guest's lifetime value.

questions.q: How do I know if a restaurant AI tool is worth keeping?
questions.a: A tool is worth keeping if it proves it saves money, drives sales or makes operations simpler. The most effective AI fits into your existing POS, scheduling and online ordering systems and removes complexity instead of adding a new dashboard to check. If it can't show that kind of payoff, it's probably a distraction.
